Resolves #21880

`examples/data/pipeline` showed the same four rows on two tabs and could not say which worker had parsed them. It is rebuilt in place around one question: what does loading and shaping a large payload cost the app? The app generates a million fictional orders as one JSON document of 97.6 MB (half a million where the device reports less than 8 GB of memory). A pipeline reads it, and the example's own interceptor turns it into a report with one row per country. The page opens with that run on the data worker; a button runs the same pipeline on the app worker, where the app itself lives. The two runs differ in one config value, `workerExecution`. Each stage shows its duration on both workers side by side, and two things show what a run cost the app: a pulse the app moves on every frame, and a heartbeat bar per run with the time the app stood still. Here that is 0.3 to 0.5 s on the app worker and nothing on the data worker.

The stage times come from the pipeline's `telemetry` sample, which lacked two things the page needs. This pull request adds them to `Neo.data.Pipeline`: the worker that ran the attempt, and the time spent in the interceptor hooks.

Evidence: L3 (browser-rendered: the spec in headless Chromium, and probes of the dev-mode page and of a production build at 1440×900 and 390×844, dark and light) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-5 and AC-7). AC-6's record is in this pull request since `#21856` merged: `data-pipeline` in `apps/portal/resources/data/examples/state.json`. Residual: the cover on neomjs/pages, from this seat, before the examples' lock.

## Deltas from ticket

- **An engine addition: two facts in the `telemetry` sample.** `worker` is `Neo.workerId` of the realm that ran the attempt. `requestStart/End`, `responseStart/End` and `postParseStart/End` time the interceptor hook chains, which ran outside the three measured stages, so with interceptors the stage times did not add up to the attempt. Additive and opt-in, as `telemetry` is. Contract Ledger and the investigation behind it: [the intake comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21880#issuecomment-7079826733). Engine lines are added and none removed: the sample had no consumer in `src/`, `apps/` or `examples/`, so nothing computed these by hand.
- **The page opens with a run, on the data worker.** The ticket describes a switch. A landing frame of empty cards read as a dead dashboard to a cold reader, and the cover is the landing frame. So the first run happens by itself, off the app worker, and the one action left to the visitor is the comparison: "Run on the app worker".
- **The shaping is the work, not the parsing.** Measured before the build: 48 MB of JSON parse in 50 to 80 ms, which no one feels. A report over the orders (a date parsed per order, distinct customers and a strongest month per country) is the kind of work that stops an app, so that is what the post-parse hook does.
- **The example's own code is an interceptor.** A pipeline in the data worker takes an app's class only as an interceptor (`modulePath`); connection, parser and normalizer are loaded by `loadDataModule`, which admits `Neo.data.*` only. Out of scope here; I file it as its own ticket.
- **A payload from memory.** The app builds the document in slices and hands the pipeline a `blob:` address, which the Fetch connection reads on either worker. Such an address takes no query string, so the request hook takes the store's paging params off. A million orders where the device reports 8 GB of memory or more, half a million elsewhere.
- **No cache stage and no marker for one.** The example configures no cache, so the sample gains nothing for it.
- **Two readings of the cost.** The heartbeat is a 5 ms timer in the App Worker; a gap of 20 ms or more between two beats is a pause, its length is the gap, and the number is their sum. A bar runs from the start of a run until 60 ms after it. The pulse is a dot the app moves every frame, for the visitor's eye: it stops for as long as the app stands still.
- **A run that does not finish** (added in the review round). A load that throws, or that resolves with nothing, is no run: the heartbeat stops, the buttons come back, the runs and samples on the page stay as they were, and a line under the payload says so. The next run builds a new pipeline. A sample counts only when its attempt was fulfilled and its store's load has brought the report: until then it is kept apart, so a store that fails after its pipeline has finished leaves no times behind.
- **The guide is not changed.** `DataPipelines.md` has no section on telemetry yet; out of scope, noted in the ticket's intake comment as the place the new fields are described.
- **The catalog record, in `state.json` since `#21856` merged** (`08e2bd3ce9`, with `order: 230`):

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dist/production` | 1440×900 | 1.2 s | 365 ms | 0 ms, 0 ms | 200 ms / 17 ms |
| `dist/production` | 390×844 | 1.2 s | 344 ms | 0 ms, 0 ms | 300 ms / 17 ms |
| dev mode | 1440×900 | 1.2 s | 358 ms | 0 ms, 0 ms | 350 ms / 17 ms |
| dev mode | 390×844 | 1.3 s | 397 ms | 0 ms, 0 ms | 233 ms / 17 ms |
| dev mode, Neo Light | 1440×900 | 1.2 s | 339 ms | 0 ms, 0 ms | 300 ms / 17 ms |

No console error and no request off the origin in any arm.

**A defect found after opening, fixed at `fb0d2e804b`.** The cover's window, 960×540, showed the report cut at the right. The theme gives a table header a minimum of 200 px, so six columns were 1,200 px wide, and the viewport clips instead of scrolling, which is why my overflow check on the document had seen nothing. The columns now share the table's width, and a phone shows three of them. The check now asks every element of the page for its right edge: none passes the window's at 1440×900, 1100×800, 960×540 and 390×844. An earlier pair of runs gave 510 and 420 ms: the number moves with the machine's load, the data worker's 0 ms did not move. The work itself costs the same on either worker, for example in the dev-mode arm at 1440×900: connection 152 ms on the app worker and 174 ms on the data worker, post-parse hook 212 ms and 222 ms. The table is from `08e2bd3ce9`, where a pause was the gap minus the 5 ms beat. At `b9d1c50b1c`, where it is the whole gap, dev mode read 335 ms on the app worker and 0 ms on the data worker at 1440×900, and 381 ms and 0 ms at 390×844, with no console error and no request off the origin in any arm.

**Specs.** `PipelineTelemetry.spec.mjs` pins the sample's keys and gains one test: with an interceptor, the six stage pairs are finite, distinct and in flow order, `worker` is the realm's id, and without a handler the three hook pairs stay `null`. Telemetry, interceptors and the CI selection: 90 of 90 at the pushed head; the six Pipeline unit specs were 92 of 92 before the rebase. `DataPipelineExample.spec.mjs`: 2 of 2, twice in a row and once more at `08e2bd3ce9`; 4 of 4 at `b9d1c50b1c` (12 s): the two runs, a load that throws, a load that brings nothing and a store that fails after its pipeline has finished (4 of 4 again at `f09628b72f`), followed by a run on the other worker and a retry, the gap boundary read in the App Worker (a gap of 19.5 ms is no pause, a gap of 20 ms is one), and the start in Neo Light.

**Mutation of the example spec.** With `workerExecution` held at `'app'` for both buttons: `the connection took time in the Data Worker`, expected > 0, received NaN. The sample names the App Worker, so the Data Worker's column stays empty.

## Cold look

One cold reader (a helper on another model, four frames of the version before this one, no source) scored it informed 6, convinced 4, excited 3. Its findings, and what the pushed head does with each:

| Finding | Pushed head |
|---|---|
| A 168 ms stall is too short to feel, and nothing on the page moves | a pulse the app moves on every frame, and a million orders: the app stands still for 0.3 to 0.5 s here and the pulse with it |
| The outcome is two small strings; "never stood still" has no number | the standstill leads each row as a number: "365 ms" and "0 ms" |
| The second run overwrites the stage cards, so "same work, different worker" is never seen | each stage shows both workers' durations side by side |
| The first frame is five "not run yet" cards and an empty table | the page opens with a finished run on the data worker |
| "Any web worker can do this": the page never shows how the location is switched | each run's row carries its config value, `workerExecution: 'app'` or `'data'`, and the instruction says that it is the one difference |
| The bars have outlined gaps, no legend, no scale | filled gaps, a legend that defines the heartbeat and a pause, and the time the full width stands for |
| "app worker", "data worker", "heartbeat", "their total", "fetched 48.8 MB" against "no request leaves it" | defined or reworded: the instruction names both workers, the legend the heartbeat, "read 97.6 MB from memory", "their count" |
| Two identical buttons, a dangling "there"; on the phone the stage cards push the result off the first screen | one primary button, a rewritten instruction, and stage rows of two lines on the phone |

Not taken: a payload-size control up to 5 million orders (about half a gigabyte of JSON in a worker); a browser Performance trace on the page (the spec and the probe are the readers that do not trust the page's own word: the pulse is read by the page's animation frames, the columns by the sample's `worker`); a real network fetch (AC-4 asks for none); stage labels on the gaps; a label on the theme button. The head `08e2bd3ce9` was read cold by the reviewer: two readers saw the 1440×900 pair of the released page and the head in opposite orders, and both preferred the head, with clarity, evidence and engagement at 8/6/8 and 9/7/8 for the head against 2/1/2 and 3/2/2 for the released page (Sophie's review 6013000720). The frames above are from the round after it, which changed two lines of text on the page and added no element to a run that finishes.
